maxIterations.description: Optimiser iterations; 0 evaluates only the initial design. Default 100.

enableOutput.description: Write optimiser output. Default true. With false the optimiser skips `optimization_data.csv` and the per-iteration forward and adjoint field output; the design and sensitivity files are always written (mma_optimizer.f90:136-137,198-205,252-257; optimizer.f90:520,547).

maxRuntime.description: Wall-clock limit as `S`, `M:S`, `H:M:S` or `D-H:M:S`; empty disables it. Default empty. The seconds-only form may be a Fortran list-directed real with a non-negative exponent (`1e3`, `5.`, `+5`, `3.6e+3`), and blanks around the string are allowed. A negative exponent (`1e-3`) aborts, because any `-` is read as the days separator. In the `M:S`, `H:M:S` and `D-H:M:S` forms the fields are plain digits here; the code also accepts list-directed forms there (`1:3e1`, `1:.5`, `+1:00:00`), which this schema does not. A duration of 0 s (`0`, `0:00`) is accepted, but the optimiser then stops after its first iteration, because the runtime-checkpoint lookup only treats a limit above 0 as enabled (optimizer.f90:342,655).
maxRuntime.$comment: optimizer.f90:428-429 calls read_duration, which trims the string and does a list-directed read of the seconds (neko src/common/utils.f90:598,662); the empty string returns early (utils.f90:499). Neko's `job_timelimit` pattern, which uses the same parser, is stricter; it is not referenced because the property path is not a $defs entry and the pattern has no empty alternative. The exponent has no `-` for the reason given above: neko src/common/utils.f90:607-612 reports 'Bad format' for `1e-3`, and optimizer.f90:429 passes no ierr, so it aborts.

stopDesignChange.description: Stop when the design change falls below this. Default machine epsilon.

restartFile.description: Optimiser checkpoint to restart from; the file must exist and end in `h5`, `hdf5` or `hf5`. At most 256 characters. Default none, but an empty value does not mean a fresh start when checkpoints of an earlier run are present: the optimiser then restarts from `<checkpoint.path>/optimizer_rt_checkpoint.h5` (only if `max_runtime` is set) or from the newest `<checkpoint.path>/<checkpoint.base>_NNNNN.h5` with NNNNN up to `max_iterations`, even when `checkpoint.interval` is <= 0 (optimizer.f90:342-376).
restartFile.$comment: optimizer.f90:1000-1012. The name is stored in character(len=256) (optimizer.f90:86) and cut silently: a longer path is looked up under its first 256 characters (optimizer.f90:435, :987, :999).

allOf.$comment: The limit is in bytes: maxLength counts code points, so non-ASCII names are not accepted (a 133-code-point name is 263 bytes).

checkpoint.description: Optimiser checkpointing. Shared by every solver (optimizer.f90:415-449).
checkpoint.$comment: path and base are stored in character(len=256) (optimizer.f90:89-90), but the file name `path + '/' + base + '_NNNNN.h5'` is built by an internal write into one character(len=256) (optimizer.f90:826-828,857-861), which aborts with 'End of record' when it is longer, in every fresh run: init_base builds it to look for earlier checkpoints (:363-366), even with checkpointing disabled. Expressed here: the default of the key that is absent (path `./checkpoints/`, 14 characters; base `optimizer_checkpoint`, 20) bounds the other. A sum of two given lengths cannot be expressed, and neither can the runtime checkpoint `optimizer_rt_checkpoint`, which with a non-empty `max_runtime` needs `path` plus a missing '/' to be at most 230 characters (:350-351).

path.description: Directory, ASCII, at most 256 bytes; the whole file name `<path>/<base>_NNNNN.h5` must fit in 256 characters (see the `$comment` of `checkpoint`). Default `./checkpoints/`.

base.description: File name base, ASCII; `<path>/<base>_NNNNN.h5` must fit in 256 characters. Default `optimizer_checkpoint`.

interval.description: Iterations between checkpoints; values <= 0 disable them. Default -1.

overwrite.description: Overwrite an existing checkpoint file (otherwise the run aborts). Default false.

continuationIterations.description: Default iterations per step of every continuation array. Default 1. A value <= 0 (without a per-key value) disables the schedule: the parameter is never updated from its array and keeps its first value (continuation_scheduler.f90:88-91,153,248).

epsimin.description: Minimum subproblem tolerance; positive and below 1. Default 1.0e-9 * sqrt(m + n). The subproblem reduces its epsilon from 1 by factors of 10 while it exceeds `epsimin`, so from 1 up (for `pdip`: from 1/0.9 up) the loop never runs and every update ignores the sensitivities (dip returns the design unchanged, pdip the midpoint of the move box). Values above about 1.0e-2 give a coarse subproblem.
epsimin.$comment: mma_cpu.f90:917-919,930,941 (dip), :502-503,516,523 (pdip); mma_device.f90:867-869,882,893 and :421,436,443. mma.f90:501-503 checks only > 0. Run on min sum(x-0.2)^2 s.t. sum x >= 1.2 (optimum 0.4): epsimin 1 dip stays at 0.5, 1.2 pdip stays at 0.5.

max_iter.$comment: The Newton loops `do iter = 1, max_iter` (mma_cpu.f90:588,984; mma_device.f90:534,936) run zero times for a value <= 0, so the subproblem is never solved: pdip keeps its start point and dip returns the midpoint of the move box (mma_cpu.f90:503), both independent of the sensitivities. mma.f90:283 does not check it.

asyinit.$comment: Iterations 1 and 2 set low/upp = x -/+ asyinit*x_diff without a clamp (mma_cpu.f90:323-326): 0 gives upp = low and the `dip` subproblem divides by upp - low (:383,:385), so the design becomes NaN; a negative value swaps the asymptotes.

backend.description: `cpu` or `device`. Default `device` in a device build, `cpu` otherwise.
backend.$comment: mma.f90:496 aborts for other values; `device` aborts in a build without a device backend (device_mma_math.f90:755).

xmin.description: Lower design bound. Default 0.0. With `xmax` absent it must not exceed the default 1.0.

xmax.description: Upper design bound. Default 1.0. With `xmin` absent it must not be below the default 0.0.

a0.description: MMA constant a0. Default 1.0. Not negative with `subsolver` `pdip` or with `a` above 0: with pdip a negative value freezes the design at the midpoint of the move box (the z-stationarity a0 - zeta - lambda.a = 0 needs zeta = a0 < 0), and with dip and a > 0 the variable z relaxes the constraints so that they end violated (mma_cpu.f90:542,609,779,966). With dip and a = 0 it is ignored.

c.description: MMA constant c, the cost of the artificial variable y. Default 1000.0. Above 0 with constraints present (rule in `optimization`), since c <= 0 leaves every constraint violated; not negative with `subsolver` `pdip`, which then freezes the design at its start (mma_cpu.f90:511,541,608,961). A small positive value does not enforce the constraints either, because c must exceed the constraint multiplier.

move_limit.description: Move limit. Values <= 0 disable it, and each update may use the whole `[xmin, xmax]` box (mma_cpu.f90:311-314, mma_device.f90:289-295). Default 0.2.

scale.description: Scaling of the constraints. Default 1.0. With constraints present it must be above 0 (or, with `auto_scale`, non-zero).

auto_scale.description: Scale by the first constraint value. Default false.

allOf.$comment: mma.f90:293-294,308-309 read the bounds and mma_cpu.f90:309-316,366-367 use them without an order check, so a lower bound above the effective upper one moves the design outside the box. Equal bounds run, hence the inclusive limits: the design stays fixed if it starts inside the box. A design that starts outside [xmin, xmax] is never projected into the box by MMA: with dip and xmin >= x0 + move_limit the move-limited box is empty and the design stays at x0, outside its bounds, for the whole run (mma_cpu.f90:309-316,323-326,366-367,978-979; run from x0 = 0 with xmin 1: 1.1e-4 against 0.4 for the default box), so a volume constraint may stay violated and the final validation abort (mma_optimizer.f90:411-414). A comparison of the bounds with the initial design cannot be expressed here.
mma_cpu.f90:511,541,608 (pdip: c + d*y - lambda - mu = 0 has no root with lambda, mu >= 0 for c < 0).
mma_cpu.f90:542,609,779 (pdip rez/delz) and :966 (dip z = max(0, 10*(lambda.a - a0))); a dip run with a = 0 ignores a0. Svanberg's MMA assumes a0 > 0.

steepestDescentSolver.description: Steepest descent. It cannot handle constraints.
steepestDescentSolver.$comment: sources/optimizer/steepest_descent_optimizer.f90:179-242. `tolerance` is read for mma only (mma_optimizer.f90:134). Constraints are rejected in the optimisation schema.

xmax.description: Upper design bound; must exceed xmin (abort at steepest_descent_optimizer.f90:215). Default 1.0.

initial.description: Initial move limit; not below `min`. Default 0.1.

max.description: Largest move limit; not below `initial`. Default 0.1.

allOf.$comment: steepest_descent_optimizer.f90:200-206,226-235 abort when initial < min or max < initial, with the defaults initial 0.1, min 0.001, max 0.1 for an absent key. A comparison of keys that are all given cannot be expressed.
steepest_descent_optimizer.f90:194-197,214-217 abort when xmin >= xmax, with the defaults xmin 0.0 and xmax 1.0 for an absent key. A comparison of two given values cannot be expressed.
